cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master's degree in Education, Counseling, Social Work, or related field.
Demonstrated experience developing, leading, and/or overseeing student support programs in a higher education setting, particularly for students with varied pathways and lived experiences.
Experience overseeing multiple programs or functional areas within a student services or student affairs unit.
Experience providing advising, counseling, or case management support to students navigating academic, financial, legal, or personal challenges.
Experience working with or coordinating services that include legal, financial, or basic needs support resources.

Knowledge of trends, policies, and issues impacting college student populations, including but not limited to undocumented students, military-connected students, re-entry students, and students with experience in foster care, housing instability, or involvement with the justice system.
Experience managing budgets, grants, or funding allocations in support of student programs or services.
Experience designing, implementing, and assessing programs or services that support student success, persistence, and well-being.
Experience developing and delivering training or educational programming for staff, faculty, or campus partners.
Experience with case management systems, student tracking, and coordinated care models.

Under the direction of the Executive Director of Retention and Validation, the Associate Director of Specialized Support Initiatives provides strategic leadership and oversight for a portfolio of programs designed to support students with varied pathways and lived experiences.

The Associate Director oversees the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of programs including Undocumented Student Services, Military-Connected Student Services, Re-entry Student Programs, and the Resilient Scholars Program. The role supervises professional staff members, ensuring coordinated, high-quality services that support student success, well-being, and degree completion.

The incumbent establishes systems and practices for program delivery, student support, and case management, including access to financial resources, legal services, and campus and community-based supports. The Associate Director serves as a key liaison to campus partners, systemwide initiatives, and external organizations, and represents the department in efforts to strengthen institutional capacity to support student success.

The position is responsible for program assessment, data-informed decision-making, and effective stewardship of resources, including budgets and funding allocations. The Associate Director contributes to departmental leadership, strategic planning, and campus-wide initiatives focused on improving student outcomes.
Familiarity with systemwide initiatives, intersegmental partnerships, or large-scale collaborative programs.
Demonstrated ability to supervise, train, and develop professional staff, including setting goals, managing performance, and fostering a collaborative team environment.
Excellent leadership and management skills.
Advanced knowledge of student development theory, counseling practices, and holistic student support approaches.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex and sensitive situations, exercise sound judgment, and coordinate appropriate interventions across multiple stakeholders.
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to collect, interpret, and use data to inform decision-making, program improvement, and reporting.
Knowledge of program evaluation methods and the ability to assess outcomes and effectiveness of services.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain collaborative relationships with campus partners, community organizations, and external stakeholders.
Knowledge of applicable federal, state, and institutional policies related to student services, including privacy, confidentiality, and ethical standards.
